subject: humanities
passage: The sitar, a long-necked instrument central to Hindustani classical music, has more strings than a listener might expect. A player plucks only six or seven main strings. A second set of thinner wires, known as sympathetic ______ beneath the main strings and vibrates on its own whenever a matching note is played, giving the sitar its ringing, shimmering tone. Most sitars have between eleven and thirteen of these wires.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject "A second set of thinner wires" goes with the verb "runs." In between, "known as sympathetic strings" is extra information. It opens with a comma after "wires," so it must close with a comma before "runs."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon would cut the subject off from its verb "runs," and neither side would be a complete sentence.
explanation.B: Correct. The closing comma matches the comma after "wires," so the subject connects to "runs."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information is never set off, and "strings runs" seems to pair a plural noun with a singular verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a comma can't close with a dash; the two marks must match.
